title: The Emperor's Secret Letter
synopsis: The Emperor's secret letter for The Hague is hidden in the palace.
Watchers stand at every gate. It must leave unseen.
goal: Find the hidden letter, take it out unseen, and give it to the envoy Yi Jun.

notes: Traces read (DeductionScene): footprints off the path toward the trees, a yellow silk thread on bark, moss pushed aside by a root all point to the old pine's hollow.

Measured 2026-11-06 on the grid sheet of c06_palace_garden.webp (picture.measuredOn): the stone lantern on the left, the garden gate, the old pine with its hollow on the right of centre, the three pots by the steps; the marks (footprints off the path, the thread on the low branch, the moss by the roots) are where the game draws them; no two areas overlap.
The traces may be drawn by the app over their areas; the picture holds no writing.
Puzzle kind chosen by hand: the season spread assigns Case 06 a trace deduction (PART 10 brief); Bongsu's note is the list of traces, each a line of it.

play.title: The Thread on the Bark
story: The Emperor's secretary hid the letter at dusk.
Then he had to leave the palace at once.
Bongsu, the errand boy, saw part of it. Where is it hidden?
play.letterIntro: A note in the King's letters, with a small water drop. Bongsu reads it to you:
play.letter:
The secretary had the Emperor's letter at dusk. Watchers came to the gate.
Footprints leave the path. They go to the trees, not to the steps.
A yellow silk thread is caught on rough bark, at hand height.
By a root, the moss is pushed aside. Someone knelt there.
— Bongsu
play.question: Where did the secretary hide the letter? Tap the place.
hints: Tap the footprints, the thread and the moss.
Which place has bark, roots, and stands among the trees?
play.successMessage: The letter is in the hollow of the old pine!
transition: In the hollow is a roll of yellow silk.
Inside is the Emperor's letter, with his seal.
"Now we must get it out," Bongsu whispers. "Past the watchers."

clue.title: The Hiding Place
clue.note: The secretary hid the Emperor's letter in the hollow of the old pine.

play.title: The Way Past the Watchers
story: The letter is under your coat now.
You remember the strangers' map of 1895. Palace paths get counted.
Bongsu knows every path. He whispers the way.
play.letter:
The watchers stand at the big front gate all day.
First, walk behind the library hall.
Do not cross the throne hall's yard: everyone sees it.
After the library, cross the garden by the old well.
Then go out by the little west gate. My uncle keeps it.
Last, walk down the lane by the stone wall.
play.question: Which way do you go? Tap the places in order.
hints: Find the words First, After, Then and Last.
Two places are watched or seen by everyone. Leave them out.
play.successMessage: You are out of the palace, unseen!
transition: Bongsu's uncle shuts the little gate behind you.
The lane is quiet. Yi Jun lives at its end.
But watchers walk this lane too.

feedback.library,well,front_gate,lane: Watchers stand at the big front gate all day. Use the little west gate.

notes: A time read in words: the watchers' walks (6:00, 6:40, 7:20) each take ten minutes; the knock comes when the 6:40 walk has passed: 6:50 (HHMM 0650). Made up.

play.title: The Watchers' Walks
story: You wait in the dark behind a cart until dawn.
Bongsu's uncle knows the watchers' times. He gives you a paper.
play.letter:
Yi Jun lives at the end of this lane.
Watchers walk past his door at 6:00, 6:40 and 7:20.
Each walk takes ten minutes.
Knock when the 6:40 walk has passed.
Do not wait for the next walk.
play.question: At what time do you knock on Yi Jun's door?
hints: How long does one walk take? Add it.
play.successMessage: At 6:50 you knock. The door opens.
transition: A tall man in a plain coat lets you in.
"I am Yi Jun," he says. "You have the Emperor's letter?"

notes: The answer is the case's key fact (h1, h2): the 1905 treaty was forced on Korea, and the envoys went to The Hague to tell the world so.
The travel box and its lock are made up; the Emperor's and Yi Jun's words are made up (dossier fiction).

clueInputs.note: The letter from the old pine is the one the envoys carry.

play.title: The Lock Word
story: Yi Jun brings out a small travel box with a letter lock.
"The Emperor chose its word," he says.
"It is what we will tell the world."
play.letterIntro: Inside the lid, Yi Jun reads:
play.letter:
THE LOCK WORD
Tell the world the truth about the 1905 treaty.
Japan made Korea sign it. Korea did not choose it.
It was not signed freely.
It was ______ on Korea.
play.question: What was the 1905 treaty? Spell the word to open the box.
hints: Read the lines inside the lid. Did Korea choose the treaty?
The word means made to happen, with no free choice.
play.successMessage: The box opens. The treaty was FORCED.
transition: Yi Jun lays the Emperor's letter in the box and locks it again.
"Thank you both," he says. "Now the world will hear us."
Bongsu folds his note and keeps it.
play.orderFeedback: All six letters fit. Japan made Korea sign it. It was ____ on Korea.

evidence.name: The Emperor's Letter, with Yi Jun
evidence.description: The Emperor's secret letter, left with the envoy Yi Jun. The envoys went to tell the world the 1905 treaty was forced.

ending.text: The letter is safe. We leave in secret.
ending.speaker: yi_jun

ending.text: The Emperor's letter, safe in your box.
In 1907, Yi Jun, Yi Sang-seol and Yi Wi-jong went to The Hague.
They went to tell the world the 1905 treaty was forced.
They reached The Hague. But they were not let into the conference.
Yi Jun died in The Hague that July.
Japan used the envoys as an excuse.
It forced the Emperor to give up his throne in 1907.
I will keep my note. One day people will read the truth.
ending.speaker: bongsu

hook: The world did not let the envoys in. Who will listen to Korea now?

objectives: Find where the letter is hidden.
Take it out past the watchers.
intro: Spring, 1907. You are a guest of Emperor Gojong at Gyeongun Palace.
In 1905, Japan forced a treaty on Korea.
Korea lost the right to deal with other countries.
This year, many countries meet at The Hague for a peace conference.
The Emperor will send three envoys there in secret.
But his secret letter is hidden, and watchers stand at every gate.
play.caseSummary: Bongsu's note led to the Emperor's letter in the old pine. It left the palace unseen and reached the envoy Yi Jun. In 1907 three envoys went to The Hague. They went to tell the world the 1905 treaty was forced. They were not let into the conference. Yi Jun died in The Hague. Japan used the envoys as an excuse to force the Emperor off his throne.
